about: What the 360 frames show along the Thames, Christchurch Bridge to Mapledurham. Positions are where the camera was; `side` is left/right of travel when heading `heading` (degrees from north). `frame` names the evidence (course:frames output).

items.name: Christchurch Bridge
items.note: 2015 foot and cycle bridge: white steel deck on one tall leaning mast with fanned cables

items.name: Caversham Bridge
items.note: 1926 road bridge: two flat concrete arches on a pier at Piper's Island, pale stone colour, balustrade parapets and lamps. Its road where the lidar puts it: the deck is 19 m wide and 8 m west of the map's line (owner, 2026-11-15)
modern brick flats, red and white, three to four storeys, across the water
the blue and white two-deck trip boat with orange lifebuoys, moored on the island side of the north channel at Piper's Island (it was placed on the main river, inside a row of tatty cruisers)
Thames Side Promenade: mown grass to the water, a line of tall trees and willows, piled edge
dense trees down to the water
big riverside houses, lawns, boathouses and landing stages on a piled edge, cruisers moored, willows
low bank lined with trees and weeping willows, open behind
trees, the odd modern house set back

one navy narrowboat near the downstream end of the moorings across from the boatyard, a small tower boat below it and a cruiser under a navy cover above it, on the passes from 2026-08-09 to 2026-11-14; on 2026-11-18 (recording 0104, a metre off) a dark narrowboat lay a little further downstream and this end of the pontoon was empty. Boats move: this is the usual layout, not one day's

cruisers upstream of it to where the surveyed row begins, some under navy or green covers (covers are drawn only on narrowboats), on every pass from 2026-08-09 to 2026-11-18 (14 passes; recording 0104): not the row of narrowboats the 2026-11-15 note made of them
overgrown banks, willows and alders, no buildings
willows, railway behind
Great Western main line on an embankment, overhead line gantries above the trees
Purley: bungalows and houses with lawns to the water, cruisers moored
flats behind lawns down to the water, weeping willows
low walls in front of the flats' lawns
concrete quay with cruisers moored along it, Fry's Island
stone and sandbag revetment, Thames Side Promenade
three tall, weathered concrete posts standing in the water off St Mary's Island, about 4 m high (pointed out by the owner)
grey-blue clapboard house with white trim behind a long stone quay: white bollards, stone urns, a white summerhouse and a white tower (pointed out by the owner)
tall red-brick boathouse: an open boat dock under a white first floor, glass balconies, a steep dark gable, white spiral stairs at both ends (pointed out by the owner)
long two-storey boathouse in pale grey: roller shutters below, a balcony on white pillars above, grey metal roof, a blue launch alongside (pointed out by the owner)
tired old cruisers below Caversham Bridge: tarps, faded paint, a flag (pointed out by the owner)
people often fish from the Promenade's stone wall here: mind their lines (pointed out by the owner)
the bank path below Mapledurham Lock, from the beach where Div 1-6 land to where they put in again (the owner's points)
modern flat-roofed house, dark glass in white frames, behind a big weeping willow, a timber edge to its lawn (pointed out by the owner)
the big weeping willow in front of the glass house
marina clubhouse, dark timber with flagpoles, and the static caravans of Riverside Park behind
a white and green wakeboard boat with a tower, at a pontoon across from the marina
the tall brick wall holding up the Great Western main line, wires and masts above (owner point 3)
a little red box on the railway wall just above the water: the owner calls it a mailbox
a big white cruiser with a navy stripe and blue fenders, opposite the wall
a timber gazebo on a deck with a ladder down to the water, behind the cruiser
maroon narrowboat with white window frames and life-size figures, one of them Lara Croft; on the left going up (owner, 2026-10-31: it was on the wrong side), the figures standing on the roof
the small white cruiser moored just above the Lara Croft boat
big white and grey clapboard houses, gables, balconies, decks and jetties (owner points 5 and 6)
a navy narrowboat at a timber pontoon with white fenders, below the red-brick houses
a blue CHANNEL sign with an arrow on a post at the water's edge, below the lock
the sandy beach where Div 1-6 land for the portage
a stepped wall of sandbags with a drain pipe, a timber deck with railings above, brick houses behind, just below the put-in
the put-in: a little beach about 10 m up from the sandbag wall, where Div 1-6 get back in (the owner: the wall blocks the water there)
a sculling club on the lawn: sculls and oars on racks beside a tall stone memorial pillar

a glass-fronted restaurant at the water with a white round tower; 10 m west of the point taken, where the lidar has its tower: with Caversham Bridge where it really is, the tower stood in the road (2026-11-15)
the ferry landing: pontoons along the hotel frontage, blue umbrellas and a flag

the bar on Piper's Island: a low white building with a long glass front and a timber deck

the Caversham Lady and the trip boats moored along Piper's Island, main channel; moved 35 m upstream, towards the bridge, so she doesn't hide the Island Bar from the main river (downstream she lay across the racing line) (owner, 2026-11-15)
town houses and flats across the open river below Piper's Island: three and four storeys, steep gables to the river, red brick with red balconies or cream render (footage 2026-08-20)
a timber boardwalk on piles along the south bank just below Christchurch Bridge, red-brown slatted fence on the water side, new flats behind (footage 2026-08-20)
a boatyard across the river: a long two-storey building, dark grey roof, pale walls with big windows and a roller door, a quay in front with cruisers moored (footage 2026-08-09, 08-12)
a big weeping willow on the north bank (footage 2026-08-12)
a second willow beside it, and taller trees (footage 2026-08-12)

a weathered timber boathouse with a deck on its roof at the water, a dense hedge of shrubs beside it (footage 2026-08-09) (moved 2026-11-16 back to where the footage and the lidar put it: in front of the villa's footprint, at the downstream end of its quay)
a big dead tree, bare grey branches, at the water's edge among the green (footage 2026-08-09, 08-14, 08-20, 08-23, 09-02)
a white sign board on a white post at the water's edge, seen from both r1 and r2 (footage 2026-08-09)
a wide bank of pale sand and gravel down to the water under a big tree (footage 2026-08-09, 08-14, 08-20, 08-23)
